question: Under the Bahmani kingdom, the provinces were administered by ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tarafdars**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under the Bahmani kingdom, the provinces were administered by **Tarafdars**.
 
• The Bahmani kingdom was a medieval Indian kingdom located in the Deccan region and was one of the great Muslim states of medieval India.
 
• The administrative structure of the Bahmani kingdom was divided into provinces, known as Tarafs, each governed by a Tarafdar.
 
• Tarafdars were responsible for maintaining law and order, collecting taxes, and overseeing the general administration of their respective provinces.
 
• This administrative division facilitated better governance and control over the extensive territories of the Bahmani kingdom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Bahmani kingdom was founded in 1347 by Ala-ud-Din Bahman Shah, who rebelled against the Sultanate of Delhi.
 
• The kingdom played a significant role in the history of Deccan India, contributing to the rich cultural and architectural heritage of the region.
 
• Over time, the Bahmani kingdom disintegrated into five smaller sultanates known as the Deccan Sultanates: Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmadnagar, Bidar, and Berar.
 
• The administrative practices of the Bahmani kingdom influenced the governance systems of these successor states.
 
• The Bahmani rulers patronized Persian culture, language, and art, which had a lasting impact on the Deccan's cultural landscape.
